Working with the seed table

seed-table.Rmd

Annotations of octo neurons live in a SeaTable table, one row per seed: a point inside a neuron, placed in Spelunker. Root IDs change whenever a neuron is proofread, but a point inside the neuron stays valid. So the table stores the position, and octor looks up the current IDs from it.

Setting up the table

Create these columns (names can be changed with the cols argument of octo_update_ids()):

Column Type Content
position Text Spelunker voxel coordinates, e.g. 11434, 13413, 2501
supervoxel_id Text Filled by octor
root_id Text Filled by octor: the current neuron ID
root_id_previous Text Previous root ID, when it changed
root_changed_on Date When the root ID last changed
ids_checked_on Date Last update
n_seeds Number How many rows share this root ID
dup_status Text unique, primary, secondary, CONFLICT ..., no segment
primary Checkbox The row you trust and fill in
same_as Text For secondary rows: position of the primary row

Keep all ID columns as Text. IDs are 64-bit integers, and Number columns silently change their last digits.

Positions can be pasted straight from Neuroglancer: 1234, 5678, 910, [1234 5678 910] and tab-separated values all work.

Updating IDs 

library(octor)
octo_update_ids(dry_run = TRUE)   # see what would change
octo_update_ids()                 # write to SeaTable

The first run looks up a supervoxel for every seed, roughly 0.3 to 1 second per point. Later runs only look up new seeds and refresh root IDs, which takes seconds. Running it daily (cron job or scheduled task) keeps the table current.

Neurons seeded more than once

When several rows point to the same root ID, they are the same neuron. In each group, one row is the primary row, the one you annotate; the others are secondary:

  • tick primary on the row you want to keep
  • if no row is ticked, octor picks the row with the most annotation filled in (cell_type, group, soma_side, reconstructor, annotator, seymour_match_id), or the oldest row if they are equal
  • CONFLICT means several rows are ticked. This usually happens when proofreading merged two neurons that were both annotated: merge the information into one row and untick the other
  • if a merged neuron is split again, its rows become unique again

Useful SeaTable views:

  • Duplicates: filter n_seeds > 1, group by root_id
  • To annotate: filter dup_status is not secondary: one row per neuron

Finding neurons 

ids <- octo_find_ids("^MBON")                     # regex on cell_type
ids <- octo_find_ids("KC", exact = TRUE)          # exactly "KC"
ids <- octo_find_ids("^L$", column = "soma_side")
seeds <- octo_seeds(trusted_only = TRUE)          # whole table, one row per neuron

Meshes 

nl <- octo_read_meshes(ids)          # 10% of faces, fast to plot
nl[, c("cell_type", "soma_side")]
rgl::plot3d(nl)

nl_full <- octo_read_meshes(ids, simplify = 1)   # full resolution

Meshes are downloaded in parallel and kept in memory for the R session, so plotting the same neurons again is instant.
